textTitles: Children’s parties — four venues in Hadley

texts.label: A
texts.title: Children’s parties — four venues in Hadley

paragraphs.text: Splash Zone at Hadley Pool. Party packages for up to twenty children aged five and over include an hour in the small pool, with an inflatable obstacle course, followed by forty minutes in the party room. Food is provided by the pool café, and a lifeguard stays with the group from start to finish. Weekend parties must be booked at least four weeks ahead.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Rolling Hills Farm. Children help to feed the lambs and goats, take a ride on a tractor trailer and finish with a picnic in the barn. You are welcome to bring your own food and birthday cake, but please tell us in advance about any allergies so that animal feed can be kept away from the picnic area. Farm parties run from April to October only.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Brightside Craft Studio. An artist shows the children how to make a clay model or paint a small canvas. Models are fired in the kiln and paintings are varnished, so the finished work is ready to collect a week after the party. Groups are limited to twelve, which makes this a good choice for younger children or a quieter celebration. We do not provide party food, but we are happy to recommend a local caterer.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Jumpworks Trampoline Park. Parties last ninety minutes and can be booked seven days a week, including evenings. A coach leads warm-up games before free jumping, and the group then has its own table in the café. Every child needs a form signed by a parent or carer before they are allowed on the trampolines, and non-slip socks, which the children keep afterwards, are included in the price.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Kestrel Ice Rink — public skating. Public sessions last two hours and start at 10 am, 1 pm and 4 pm every day. On Fridays and Saturdays there is an extra session from 7.30 pm to 9.30 pm, when music is played and the lights are turned down. The rink is closed to the public on Tuesday mornings for ice hockey training and occasionally at other times for competitions; these closures are shown on our website at least a week in advance.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Admission is £8 for adults and £6 for children under fourteen, including the hire of skates. Skaters who bring their own skates pay £1.50 less. Everyone on the ice must wear gloves, and helmets are strongly recommended for children. Both can be bought at the reception desk, and helmets may also be borrowed free of charge. Children under eight must be accompanied on the ice by a paying adult.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Beginners may use plastic skating frames, which help them to keep their balance. There is a small stock by the rink entrance; frames cannot be reserved and are handed out in the order that people arrive. Food and drink may not be taken onto the ice. Lockers are provided in the changing area, and lost property is kept for one month. Group lessons for beginners take place on Sunday mornings before the first public session; places are limited and must be booked online.
paragraphs.label: C
